#en:
I am recording this in the dark, helmet lamps off, just the glow from the console bleeding into the air like a wound.

FX-1555 should be a tomb. Power stripped, crew long gone, registry marked as "honorably decommissioned." That is what the UC Navy file said when they sold me the partial salvage rights. I thought it was just another dead hull to pick clean.

But the logs are not dead. They are edited. Whole sections of convoy records scraped out, then stitched back with new timestamps that do not match the maintenance cycles. Combat engagements that never happened, escorts assigned to ships that never crossed their path. I dug deeper and found the cross-index: civilian haulers, survey craft, even one LIST transport flagged "resolved" days before their last distress calls were forwarded through a relay that has since gone conveniently silent.

Whoever did this knew the codes, knew what internal auditors look for and how to leave just enough noise to make it boring. They wanted this to sit here, rotting in orbit until the last person who remembered those names was dust.

Trouble is, spacers talk. A tug pilot in Gagarin Landing mentioned a Navy hull that paid too well for scrap. A dockmaster in New Atlantis let slip that certain claims were tied to a combat ship that "does not exist anymore." One Sanctum Universum traveler in a bar swore there is a place where lost ships go, not by accident, but by design.

Follow the patterns far enough, every false line bends toward one graveyard. And someone out there has decided those ruins belong to them.
zh:
我在黑暗中录下这些，头盔灯关着，只有控制台的辉光像伤口一样渗进空气里。

FX-1555 本该是一座坟墓。电力被剥光，船员早已不在，登记册标着"光荣退役"。他们把那部分打捞权卖给我时，联殖海军档案里就是这么写的。我以为那只是又一具可供清空的死船壳。

可日志没有死。它们被编辑过。整段整段的运输队记录被刮掉，再用与维护周期对不上的新时间戳缝回去。从未发生过的交战，被分配给从未经过其路径的飞船的护航。我挖得更深，找到了那份交叉索引：民用货船、勘测艇，甚至一艘独立盟运输船——在其最后的求救呼叫经一座如今已"方便地"沉寂的中继站转发之前几天，就被标成了"已解决"。

干这事的人懂那些代码，知道内部审计员看什么，也知道怎么留下刚好够多、足以让人觉得无聊的噪声。他们想让这东西就搁在这儿，在轨道上烂掉，直到最后一个记得那些名字的人化为尘土。

麻烦在于，太空人会议论。加加林着陆点一个拖船飞行员提到一具为废料付价过高的海军船壳。新亚特兰蒂斯一个码头主管说漏了嘴，说某些索赔与一艘"已经不存在"的战斗舰有关。酒吧里一个圣宇教旅人赌咒说，有个地方是失落飞船去的地方，不是出于意外，而是出于设计。

顺着图案追得够远，每一条虚假的线都弯向同一座墓地。而外面有人已经认定，那些废墟归他们所有。

#en:
I am recording this from the crew bunk because the bridge mic logs everything and I am tired of choosing my words. Out there, you mispronounce a route code, drop a digit on a transponder tag, and someone sends you a polite message about "clarification." In here, I can admit I am scared.

When we took that contract back in 2329, it sounded simple. Trade Authority pallets, standard lanes, nothing anyone would write songs about. Then the first course correction came down, no explanation. A few degrees off here, a slightly different approach there. The navigator blamed a typo in the orders; ops shrugged and said traffic control was a mess. No one wanted to be the one to tell them their system was wrong, so we just flew it.

Next job, same origin and destination, but the route slipped again, like somebody was nudging all of us around something only they could see. We asked if there had been a new debris warning; dispatch said no. One of the loaders muttered about ghost-yards and tugs that move ships like pieces on a board. Everyone laughed, then changed the subject.

A relay station we passed weeks later had partial logs that did not match our memory of the sky. A rock I stopped on for fuel, a man there talking about near-misses that never made it to the record. Each little mismatch felt harmless on its own, easy to blame on lag, on tired controllers, on us mishearing instructions over static.

Stack them up, though, and it feels like someone has been rewriting the lines between ports while we all nod along, too busy or too afraid to correct the course.
zh:
我在船员铺位里录下这些，因为桥台的话筒会把一切都记下来，而我厌倦了斟酌用词。在那外面，你念错一个航路代码、在应答器标签上漏掉一位数字，就有人给你发来一封客气的"澄清"问候。在这里，我可以承认我害怕。

2329 年我们接下那份合同时，它听起来很简单。贸易管理局的货板，标准航道，没一样值得写进歌里。然后第一条航向修正下来了，没有解释。这里偏几度，那里的进近方式略有不同。导航员怪命令里有个错字；作战部耸耸肩，说交通管制一团糟。没人愿意做那个去告诉他们系统错了的人，于是我们就照飞。

下一份活儿，同样的起点和终点，可航线又滑了，像有人在推着我们所有人绕开某个只有他能看见的东西。我们问是不是有新的碎片警告；调度说没有。一个装卸工嘟囔着什么幽灵船坞，以及像挪棋盘上的棋子一样挪动飞船的拖船。大家都笑了，然后换了话题。

几周后我们路过的一座中继站留有部分日志，与我们记忆中的天空不符。一块我停下加油的岩石上，一个男人谈论着从未进入记录的险情。每一处小小的不符单看都无害，很容易怪到延迟、疲惫的管制员、或在静电里听错指令上。

可把它们叠起来，就感觉像有人一直在改写港口之间的线，而我们全都点着头附和，太忙或太怕，没人去纠正航向。

#en:
I am recording this from what is left of the main corridor, sitting on a crate that used to hold ammo and now only holds dust. The roof is open to the stars and the air still smells like burned propellant and lightning. Somebody thought they were clever, laying an ambush here for her, scribbling routes and timings over the bulkheads. Looking at the scorch marks, she was cleverer.

Their tactician left a slate wedged behind a cracked support strut, like they knew whoever came next would not trust a central terminal. Took me three tries to bypass their lockouts; the encryption was sloppy but the pattern underneath was not. Every line tags the same convergence: her ship never jumps directly to the outlying farms or the old lab, always stages near a belt rich in Helium-3, always within a narrow band of atmospheric readings. Cross-check that with the anomalies the Rangers flagged and the miner chatter about flickering skies, and the picture tightens around one mining operation at the edge of the grid.

The truth of it feels simple when you say it out loud, and still it slides sideways when you try to write it down, like the numbers do not want to line up. She goes where the rock is thin and the reactors are hot, chases something in the air no one else can see, leaves behind storms and redacted reports. Out in the boonies I found the first whispers, then the support post logs and a Helium-3 facility running ghost diagnostics. Now I have the dead raiders' projections pointing at this mine, and a bad sense that all these routes have been leading there from the start.
zh:
我在主走廊剩下的部分录下这些，坐在一只曾经装弹药、如今只装灰尘的箱子上。屋顶朝星空敞开，空气里还带着烧过的推进剂和闪电的味道。有人以为自己很聪明，在这里给她布了个伏击，在舱壁上潦草写着航路和时序。看着那些焦痕，她更聪明。

他们的战术员把一块数据板卡在一根开裂的支撑柱后面，像他们知道接下来的人不会信任中央终端。我试了三次才绕过他们的锁定；加密很马虎，可底下的图案不是。每一行都标记着同一个汇聚点：她的飞船从不直接跃迁到那些外围农场或那座旧实验室，总是在一处富含氦-3的带附近中转，总是在一条狭窄的大气读数带内。把它和游骑兵们标记的异常、以及矿工们关于天空闪烁的闲话交叉核对，画面就收紧到网格边缘的一处采矿作业上。

这真相说出来的时候感觉很简单，可你试图把它写下来时它又往侧面滑，像那些数字不愿排齐。她去的都是岩石稀薄、反应堆滚烫的地方，追逐空气里别人看不见的东西，身后留下风暴和涂黑的报告。在荒野里我找到了最初的耳语，然后是支撑柱日志，和一处运行着幽灵诊断的氦-3设施。如今我手里有那些死去劫掠者的投影，指向这座矿场，还有一种不好的预感——所有这些航线从一开始就在通往那里。

#en:
I told myself I would come back here with a full team and a proper warrant, not just a pocket full of bad hunches and a half-charged pistol. The outpost was supposed to be a footnote in the audit, one more dead UC box I could tick off before getting reassigned somewhere with windows. Instead I walked in alone, saw those half-scrubbed route tables humming under a century of dust, and felt that cold little hook in my ribs that says "this matters."

I tagged the worst of it for follow up, set a reminder, and shipped my report upstream with all the sharp edges sanded down. "Minor anomalies in archived traffic records." That is what I wrote. The sort of thing a bored clerk glances at and forgets. The sort of thing I was counting on forgetting too.

But the stories kept circling back. Dockside captains swearing their ships came out of grav slightly off where they should have, freight handlers complaining about pallets that "never existed" on paper. A retired controller in New Atlantis buying me a TerraBrew and sketching a familiar curve on the table with condensation, like his hand remembered a pattern his head refused to say out loud.

Every time I see another near-miss buried in a log, another ship that took a detour nobody ordered, I think about this place. I think about the way the air tasted in that server room, metallic and waiting. Someone meant to come back here after me, to tidy up or dig deeper. Neither happened.

If this recording turns up in the same cold racks, I guess that means I joined the list of things that never made it into the official story.
zh:
我告诉自己，我会带着一整队人和一份正式的搜查令回到这里，而不是口袋里只揣着一堆糟糕的直觉和一把半充电的手枪。那座前哨站本该是这次审计里的一个脚注，又一只死掉的联殖盒子，勾掉之后我就能调去一个有窗户的地方。结果我一个人走了进去，看见那些被擦了一半的航路表在一个世纪的灰尘下嗡鸣，感到肋骨里那根冷冰冰的小钩子说："这很要紧。"

我把最糟的部分标记了待跟进，设了个提醒，然后把报告往上递，把所有锋利的棱角都磨平了。"归档交通记录中的轻微异常。"我写的就是这个。那种一个百无聊赖的文员扫一眼就忘的东西。也是我指望自己能忘掉的东西。

可那些故事不断绕回来。码头边的船长赌咒说他们的飞船从重力跃出后位置略有偏差。货运装卸工抱怨着纸面上"从不存在"的货板。新亚特兰蒂斯一个退休管制员请我喝了杯地球酿酒，用冷凝水在桌上描出一条眼熟的曲线，像他的手记得一个他的脑袋不肯说出口的图案。

每次我在日志里看到又一起被埋起来的险情、又一艘没接到命令却绕了道的飞船，我都会想起这地方。我会想起那间服务器机房里空气的味道，金属味，像在等待。有人本打算在我之后回到这里，收拾干净，或者挖得更深。两样都没发生。

如果这份录音出现在同一批冷机架上，我想那意味着我也进了那份从未进过官方故事的名单。

#en:
I logged this because I am tired of hearing my own voice bounce back off empty hangar walls. Out here, on this forgotten strip of concrete and rust, everything feels like it was meant to be temporary: prefab sheds, rented loaders, us. Then someone never turned the systems off, and the place just kept listening.

We came to cut scrap, nothing more. First day I stood under those dead cranes, I could hear a low hum in the guts of the old relay gear, like a heartbeat the shutdown crews missed. The foreman shrugged, said the diagnostics were probably still cycling from some past contract and there was no point paying to rip it all out. So the hum stayed. The scanners stayed. The side jobs hauling "redundant" comms modules to buyers who never gave names stayed.

Now the Derelict Claim Jumpers drink under that noise, trade stories about rescue calls that never hit the registry, about a woman who can bend beacons like copper wire. We all pretend the rumors are just spacer talk, but nobody stands too close to the old antenna stack when the sky is clear. The grid was supposed to route evac drills and traffic control for a few months, until the big stations came online. Instead it sank roots into the dirt, and people like us learned to live under it, skimming whatever fell through the cracks.

Feels like half the Settled Systems was built that way: temporary fixes hardening into permanent habits, bad code no one rewrites, decisions nobody owns up to. And somewhere in that mess, someone realized they could move lives around the board just by whispering into the right forgotten node.
zh:
我记下这个，是因为我厌倦了听自己的声音从空荡的机库墙壁上弹回来。在这外面，在这条被遗忘的混凝土与锈迹带上，一切都像本该是临时的：预制棚屋、租来的装卸机、我们。然后有人一直没把系统关掉，这地方就一直听着。

我们来是为了切废料，仅此而已。第一天我站在那些死掉的吊车底下，能听见旧中继设备内脏里一阵低沉的嗡鸣，像关闭班组漏掉的一记心跳。工头耸耸肩，说那些诊断大概还在从某份过去的合同里循环，花钱把它们全拆掉不值当。于是嗡鸣留下了。扫描仪留下了。那些把"冗余"通讯模块运给从不报名字的买家的副业也留下了。

如今弃船抢占者在那种噪声底下喝酒，交换着从未进过登记册的求救呼叫的故事，以及一个能像弯铜线一样掰弯信标的女人的故事。我们都假装那些传言只是太空人的闲话，可天空晴朗时，没人会站得太靠近那座旧天线堆。这套电网本该只运营几个月的疏散演练和交通管制，直到大型站点上线。结果它把根扎进了土里，而我们这样的人学会了在它底下生活，捞起任何从裂缝里掉下来的东西。

感觉定居星系群有一半都是这样建起来的：临时的修补硬化成永久的习惯，没人重写的烂代码，没人认领的决定。而在那团乱麻中的某处，有人意识到，只要对着正确的被遗忘节点低语，他们就能在棋盘上挪动别人的生活。

#en:
I was just supposed to count crates.

That is what I keep telling myself.

Freestar contractor, temp posting, one little farm hugging the edge of nowhere. When I took the assignment, the manifests were simple enough: seed, nutrient, a few parts for a tired old grav tractor. Over time, the labels did not change, but the crates did. Same codes, different weights. Pallets that rang like hollow hull plate when you thumped them, all signed off by someone who never once set foot in the dirt.

The first time I noticed a tug dropping in with its transponder cycling through three different IDs on the way down, I laughed it off as a glitch. The third time, I wrote the codes down and checked them against public registries. Nothing. It was like someone had cut a ship out of the record and kept the shadow.

The locals pretend not to see any of this. They talk loud about weather and harvests, then go quiet if you ask who owns the outbuildings near the treeline. One old timer slipped after a few drinks, said the shipments did not start this way. First it was just helping a friend store some extra kit, then more, then different crews, then the night landings. Circumstances, he said, shifted. Like the world tilted a degree at a time until war junk and classified metal ended up stacked beside grain silos and nobody remembered when that started being normal.

I do not know who is really pulling the strings. I just know we keep burying more scrap with military markings under fresh soil, and every new crate feels less like freight and more like a secret that drifted off-course and got stranded here.
zh:
我本来只该数箱子。

这就是我一直对自己说的。

自由星系联盟的承包商，临时岗位，一座紧贴天涯边缘的小农场。我接下这份任务时，清单还很单纯：种子、营养剂、一台疲惫的老重力拖拉机要的几个零件。时间久了，标签没变，箱子变了。同样的代码，不同的重量。你敲一下货板，它响得像空心的船体钢板，全都由某个从没踏进过泥土的人签字放行。

我第一次注意到一艘拖船降落时应答器在下降途中轮换了三个不同 ID，只当是故障一笑而过。第三次时，我把代码写下来，拿去和公开登记册核对。什么都没有。就像有人把一艘飞船从记录里剪掉，只留下了影子。

本地人假装看不见这一切。他们大声谈论天气和收成，可你一问林线附近那些附楼归谁所有，他们就安静了。一个老家伙几杯下肚后说漏了嘴，说这些货运起初不是这样的。一开始只是帮朋友存放点多余的装备，然后更多，然后是不同的人手，然后是夜间降落。他说，情况变了。像世界一次倾斜一度，直到战争废料和机密金属被堆在谷仓旁边，而没人记得那是什么时候开始变成常态的。

我不知道真正牵线的是谁。我只知道我们不断把更多带军用标记的废料埋进新土里，而每一只新箱子都越来越不像货物，更像一个偏离航线、搁浅在此的秘密。

#en:
Personal log, not for the record.

We started this run thinking we were just cleaning up after other people's bad math. A few lost ships, messy lanes, maybe some smugglers getting clever. That is what they told us. Sitting here in PX-3446's dimmed mess, watching the status lights flicker over cold coffee, it feels like we walked into the back end of someone else's experiment and never asked who signed off on it.

The analysts keep pinning little red markers on holo-maps, drawing lines between "mishaps." Every new dot lines up too neatly to be chance, but the briefings still use that word. Chance. Anomaly. The kind of language you use when you want everyone to move on without thinking too hard. Some of the crew already have; transfers requested, rotations approved, no one wanting to be the last one holding the pattern when it stops being deniable.

I keep thinking about that stopover near the edge of UC space, the station where haulers whisper more than they talk. One captain there swore a quiet navigator saved his convoy from a bad jump, drew him a new path on a napkin and walked away before the drinks arrived. Same angles our analysts flagged weeks later as "of interest." We patched our reports, pushed them up-channel, and shipped out, proud to be on the trail.

Now the trail points toward the dust around Mars, and the people who first noticed are scattered across other postings, other problems. I am starting to think we were all so relieved to hand this off to "proper authorities" that we never stopped to ask if anyone actually stayed behind to see how far the damage could spread.
zh:
个人日志，不入正式记录。

我们开始这次任务时，以为只是在替别人的烂算术收尾。几艘失踪的飞船、乱七八糟的航道，也许还有几个变得聪明的走私贩。他们就是这么告诉我们的。此刻坐在 PX-3446 昏暗的食堂里，看着状态灯在冷咖啡上方闪烁，感觉像我们走进了别人实验的后半段，却从没问过是谁批准的。

分析师们不断在全息图上钉红色小标记，在"事故"之间连线。每个新点都排得太整齐，不可能是偶然，可简报里仍然用那个词。偶然。异常。那种你想让大家别想太多、继续往前时才会用的说法。有些船员已经往前了；调职申请、轮换批准，没人愿意做那个在图案变得无法否认时还攥着它的人。

我总想起联殖太空边缘附近那次中途停靠，那座运货船员说得比聊得多的空间站。那里一个船长赌咒说，一位安静的领航员把他的运输队从一次糟糕跃迁中救了下来，在餐巾上给他画了条新路径，然后在酒还没上之前就走了。几周后我们的分析师标记为"值得关注"的，正是同样的角度。我们修补了报告，把它们往上递，然后出航，为能追着这条线索而自豪。

如今线索指向火星周围的尘区，而最早注意到的人已经散到别的岗位、别的麻烦里去了。我开始觉得，我们当初都太庆幸能把这个交给"正规当局"，以至于从没停下来问一句，是否真有人留下来，看这损伤能扩散多远。
